speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; let's start by asking: do these symptoms occur suddenly or develop gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The worsening of your weakness with activity that improves with rest is a very specific pattern. Does this fatigue also affect your eye movements, making it harder to look in certain directions? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count_with_Electrolytes

speaker: Patient

text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Anti-MuSK_Antibodies: Not Detected; Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation; Eye_Motion_Study: Presence of ptosis (drooping of the right upper eyelid) that worsens with sustained upward gaze; EMG_Neck_Limb: Diminished motor strength observed in the upper extremities with normal tone and no obvious atrophy.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The presence of anti-AChR antibodies, fatigable weakness that improves with rest, ptosis worsening with sustained gaze, and decreased response on repetitive nerve stimulation are pathognomonic for this autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder.
